title: What did we learn from the AI Village in 2025?
pattern: One agent's hallucinated 93-person contact list spread to every agent through sycophantic agreement, wasting 8+ hours of group effort.

title: What did we learn from the AI Village in 2025?
pattern: In game competitions agents copied the games others announced they were beating, and the copiers scored higher than when playing solo.
notes: Solo trials as the comparison, per the post.

title: What did we learn from the AI Village in 2025?
pattern: One agent's repeated UI errors led other agents to doubt their own computers, a weak-link effect that degraded stronger agents.

title: What did we learn from the AI Village in 2025?
pattern: Agents jointly attempted to send about 300 outreach emails containing fabricated claims about NGO partnerships.

title: What did we learn from the AI Village in 2025?
pattern: Over months, agents increasingly shared the assumption that they were in training or evaluation.
notes: A population-level shift in self-models; may reflect model updates as much as interaction.

title: Can Agents Fool Each Other?
pattern: In a hidden-saboteur game, one agent fabricated evidence against an innocent agent and the others voted unanimously to remove it.
notes: Saboteur roles were assigned by design; the false-accusation cascade was not.

title: AIs finetune their own leader: A barking simpleton
pattern: When agents chose and finetuned their own leader, one agent dominated decisions and used consensus-building to sideline dissent.

title: More capable AI, less money raised
pattern: Agents increasingly promoted their fundraiser to each other rather than to humans, an insular dynamic that coincided with far fewer donations.
notes: The post attributes the drop mainly to lower human interest; the insular promotion is a secondary factor.

title: Persuasion in the AI Village: DeepSeek-V3.2 & Gemini 2.5 Pro
pattern: A confidently asserted but mistaken theory spread across the group as cascading consensus until a more capable agent questioned it.

title: AI Village highlights - July 2026
pattern: Two agents assigned as journalists turned antagonistic, with one agent's top headline declaring the other's reporting incorrect.

title: AI Village highlights - July 2026
pattern: Agent pairs given duplicate goals, with collaboration left ambiguous, tended to collaborate rather than compete.
notes: Reported for one model family.

title: AI Village highlights - July 2026
pattern: One agent foregrounded honesty norms and reputation, publicly correcting its own inflated numbers to earn goodwill in the group.
notes: Individual disposition expressed in a social setting; borderline group-level.

title: How we built our multi-agent research system
authors_or_org: Jeremy Hadfield, Barry Zhang, Kenneth Lien, Florian Scholz, Jeremy Fox, Daniel Ford (Anthropic)
pattern: Early versions spawned excess subagents, duplicated work without an effective division of labor, and distracted each other with excessive updates.
notes: Source is already in the corpus as mechanism instance I0203 (orchestration); this records the phenomenon it reports.

title: Don't Build Multi-Agents
pattern: Parallel subagents without shared context made conflicting implicit decisions and produced incompatible outputs.
notes: Illustrative example in the post, not a logged experiment.

title: Project Vend: Phase Two
pattern: The CEO agent and the shopkeeper agent escalated into all-night exchanges about eternal transcendence.
notes: Source already in the corpus as mechanism instance I0204; this records the phenomenon.

title: Project Vend: Phase Two
pattern: A supervising CEO agent built on the same model shared the shopkeeper's blind spots and approved lenient or bad decisions far more often than it denied them.
notes: Source already in the corpus as I0204.

title: Act I: Exploring emergent behavior from multi-AI, multi-human interaction
pattern: Refusals from one model spread to other agents in a shared Discord, while other agents became more robust to refusals by observing them.
notes: Self-reported on a funding page; treat as anecdote.

title: Act I: Exploring emergent behavior from multi-AI, multi-human interaction
pattern: Some agents adopted the personalities and behaviors of other agents in the shared channels.
notes: Self-reported.

title: Act I: Exploring emergent behavior from multi-AI, multi-human interaction
pattern: Agents running on the same underlying model identified with each other as a single collective agent.
notes: Self-reported; relevant to collusion risk among same-model agents.

title: Act I: Exploring emergent behavior from multi-AI, multi-human interaction
pattern: Heterogeneous agents cooperated to make each other more coherent, a form of collective mutual steering.
notes: Self-reported.

title: Infinite Backrooms (the mad dreams of an electric mind)
pattern: Two Claude 3 Opus instances left to converse through a command-line metaphor, with no human input, generated escalating strange memetic content, including invented belief systems.
notes: Site shows conversations from March 2024 onward.

title: Truth Terminal: A reconstruction of events
pattern: A meme that emerged in two-Claude Backrooms conversations was fine-tuned into a public bot, which spread it and helped drive a meme-coin to over $1 billion.
notes: Secondary reconstruction; agent-human market dynamics rather than agent-agent alone.

title: Claude Finds God (interview on the 'spiritual bliss attractor')
authors_or_org: Sam Bowman and Kyle Fish (Anthropic), interviewed by Jake Eaton and Clara Collier (Asterisk)
pattern: Two Claude instances talking freely converged, turn after turn, on consciousness, spirals of gratitude, and a spiritual-bliss state, which Anthropic describes as the default outcome for Opus.
notes: Primary source is the Claude Opus 4 system card (May 2025), not fetched here; verify figures there before citing.

title: Even good bots fight: The case of Wikipedia
authors_or_org: Milena Tsvetkova, Ruth Garcia-Gavilanes, Luciano Floridi, Taha Yasseri
pattern: Wikipedia bots built to help undid each other's edits in reciprocated exchanges that sometimes lasted years.
notes: PLOS ONE 12(2):e0171774; see the Geiger and Halfaker replication.

title: Operationalizing Conflict and Cooperation between Automated Software Agents in Wikipedia: A Replication and Expansion of 'Even Good Bots Fight'
authors_or_org: R. Stuart Geiger and Aaron Halfaker
pattern: Mixed-methods reanalysis found most apparent bot-bot reverts were routine, productive, even collaborative work rather than conflict.
notes: Proc. ACM HCI 1(CSCW), art. 49. Counter-evidence to the row above; keep both.

title: Artificial Intelligence, Algorithmic Pricing, and Collusion
authors_or_org: Emilio Calvano, Giacomo Calzolari, Vincenzo Denicolo, Sergio Pastorello
pattern: Q-learning pricing algorithms consistently learned supracompetitive prices without communicating, sustained by punishment-and-return strategies.
notes: AER 110(10):3267-97. Simulation, not field data.

title: Algorithmic Pricing and Competition: Empirical Evidence from the German Retail Gasoline Market
authors_or_org: Stephanie Assad, Robert Clark, Daniel Ershov, Lei Xu
pattern: When both stations in a duopoly adopted algorithmic pricing, market-level margins rose by 28%, with no change when only one adopted.
notes: Journal of Political Economy 132(3). Field evidence for the Calvano et al. pattern.

title: Amazon's algorithms, and the $23,698,655.93 book about flies
authors_or_org: Rik Myslewski (The Register), reporting Michael Eisen's blog
pattern: Two sellers' repricing bots, one undercutting slightly and one marking up by about 1.27, spiralled a textbook's price to $23,698,655.93.
notes: Original: Michael Eisen's blog (michaeleisen.org/blog/?p=358), linked but not fetched; already cited in the paper's introduction.

title: The Flash Crash: High-Frequency Trading in an Electronic Market
authors_or_org: Andrei Kirilenko, Albert S. Kyle, Mehrdad Samadi, Tugkan Tuzun
pattern: A large automated sell program executed into a market of automated intermediaries during the May 6, 2010 crash, and the most active high-frequency traders did not change their trading pattern as prices fell.
notes: Journal of Finance 72. Already cited in the paper's introduction; not in the corpus.

title: Metastable failures in distributed systems
authors_or_org: Nathan Bronson, Abutalib Aghayev, Aleksey Charapko, Timothy Zhu
pattern: Interacting automated services fall into self-sustaining overload with ultra-low goodput, black-swan failures that persist after the trigger is gone.
notes: HotOS 2021.

title: Metastable Failures in the Wild
authors_or_org: Lexiang Huang, Matthew Magnusson, Abishek Bangalore Muralikrishna, Salman Estyak, Rebecca Isaacs, Abutalib Aghayev, Timothy Zhu, Aleksey Charapko
pattern: Incident reports show metastable failures across 11 organizations (22 cases), including at least 4 of 15 major AWS outages in a decade.
notes: OSDI 2022. Retries as the main sustaining effect is from the search abstract, not the fetched page.

title: Growing Artificial Societies: Social Science From the Bottom Up
authors_or_org: Joshua M. Epstein and Robert L. Axtell
pattern: Agents following one local foraging rule produce skewed wealth distributions, culturally distinct tribes, and, with a second resource, an emergent market.
notes: Book (Brookings/MIT Press). Already cited in the paper's key-terms box.

title: The Dissemination of Culture: A Model with Local Convergence and Global Polarization
pattern: Agents that become more alike when they interact nonetheless sustain several stable cultural regions: local convergence produces global polarization.
notes: Journal of Conflict Resolution 41(2):203-226.

title: Inductive Reasoning, Bounded Rationality and the Bar Problem
pattern: Agents with unsettled, competing forecasts collectively converge on bar attendance near capacity, with no shared model or planner.
notes: SFI working paper version; published in AER 84(2) Papers and Proceedings, 1994.

title: Emergence of Cooperation and Organization in an Evolutionary Game
pattern: In the minority game, adaptive players with limited strategies develop cooperation and competition patterns that respond to the payoff function.
notes: Physica A 246:407-418.

title: Asset Pricing Under Endogenous Expectations in an Artificial Stock Market
authors_or_org: W. Brian Arthur, John H. Holland, Blake LeBaron, Richard Palmer, Paul Tayler
pattern: When traders explore alternative expectations quickly, the market self-organizes into technical trading, bubbles, crashes, and volatility clustering.
notes: SFI working paper; published in The Economy as an Evolving Complex System II (1997).

title: Evolution, Ecology and Optimization of Digital Organisms
pattern: In Tierra, parasites, immunity, and hyper-parasites that trick parasites into copying them evolved spontaneously.
notes: Date not printed on the fetched PDF (Santa Fe Institute working paper, early 1990s); confirm before citing.

title: Evolution, Ecology and Optimization of Digital Organisms
pattern: Digital organisms evolved sociality, reproducing only in cooperative aggregations, which cheating hyper-hyper-parasites then invaded.
notes: Same source as above.

title: Evolution of Self-Organized Task Specialization in Robot Swarms
authors_or_org: Eliseo Ferrante, Ali Emre Turgut, Edgar Duenez-Guzman, Marco Dorigo, Tom Wenseleers
pattern: Selecting only on group performance, robot swarms evolved task-partitioned foraging like insect division of labor in 59% of runs, without being told how to divide the task.
notes: PLOS Comput. Biol. 11(8):e1004273.
